title: Trace: one client, two rectangles

questions.prompt: The demo's rectangle has opposite corners (2, 1) and (9, 4). What should report return as (area, perimeter)?

choices.why: That treats the far corner's coordinates 9 and 4 as the side lengths. The sides are differences of coordinates.
The sides are 9 - 2 = 7 and 4 - 1 = 3, so the area is 21 and the perimeter is 2 × (7 + 3) = 20.
The area is right, but a perimeter counts all four sides, not one width and one height.

checklist.step: A corner rectangle that answers through point selectors only
One report that serves any rectangle, one read per selector
Frames for each read, then the report

hints: Each layer may know how the layer directly beneath it is stored, and nothing further down.
Follow one call of report downwards: which function touches the rectangle's storage, and which touches a point's?
Store the two corners. A side length is the absolute difference of two coordinates read with x_point or y_point. report multiplies and adds the two numbers its selectors return.
